crime: Every evening until lockup a girl played pool alone in the recreation room, never looking up from a shot for anyone.

At the upper railing {WITCH_NAME} smelled what each girl craved and handed it over unasked; each laughed that it was just right. Nightly at half past nine she left the pool player a treat inside the door, unthanked.

At half past seven {WITCH_NAME} told the pool player it was her birthday and cried. Without looking up from her shot, the girl pressed a lemon drop into her hand: "There. All better." She smelled only of cue chalk.

{WITCH_NAME} had cried at her eighth birthday party because nobody asked what she wished for. Her mother pressed a lemon drop into her hand, "There. All better," and turned back to the guests. A sweet is what you give so you don't have to look.

At nine she returned to the recreation room and took a cue from the rack. The player was reaching into a pocket for the white ball. From behind, {WITCH_NAME} pulled the cue back across her throat until the girl went still, then laid her over the far rail as if lining up a shot, back to the door, cue by her bridge hand.

From quarter past nine she stood with the others at the railing in the second-floor hall. At half past nine she said the pool player craved a lemon drop and set one inside the door; the girls beside her saw the player bent over the pool table. She stayed until lockup.
At five to ten the prisoners found the player strangled over the far rail. At trial they ruled someone killed her after half past nine, when {WITCH_NAME} was at the railing with them.

A prisoner opened the right hand pinned under the girl's chest. It still gripped the white ball; she had never picked her cue back up. She had died fetching the white ball before half past nine; {WITCH_NAME} had invented the craving.
fields.epitaph: She never wanted the sweet, only for someone to look up.
fields.epithet: A Sweet Instead of a Look
execution: A birthday cake as tall as the trial court rises. Lit candles, each taller than she is, ring its top tier, and she stands alone at its center.
She crouches with her arms over her head as the candles soften and bow inward until their flames meet on her.
They burn down into the icing. Smoke rises from the still figure crouched at their center.

magic.name: Scent of Longing
magic.text: She can smell what anyone near her secretly longs for, as the scent of that very thing.
